entry.title: ITEM_2019B Corp Fin 03SXL 09U1
entry.itemBody:
An analyst gathers the following information (in £ millions) about a company:

Cash 50
Short-term marketable investments 37
Receivables 15
Current assets 114
Current liabilities 100

The quick ratio of this company is closest to:

answerFeedback.0e3f4d21-f2d3-487f-9473-94e373707846:
Correct because the quick ratio (also known as the acid-test ratio) is the ratio of the quick assets to current liabilities. Quick assets are those assets that can be most readily converted to cash.
Quick ratio = (Cash + Short-term marketable investments + Receivables)/Current liabilities" = (50 + 37 + 15)/100 = 1.02.
answerFeedback.597571a6-dc1c-4ca7-b87a-0b3c902a12b8:
Incorrect because the current ratio is calculated, not the quick ratio.
Quick ratio ≠ Current assets/Current liabilities = 114/100 = 1.14.
answerFeedback.8b9841bd-a75c-47c1-944a-fecdf3bee4e1:
Incorrect because receivables are not included (in the numerator) when calculating the quick assets.
Quick ratio ≠ (Cash + Short-term marketable investments)/Current liabilities = (50 + 37)/100 = 0.87.

entry.title: ITEM_2019B Corp Fin 11LFW 09U3
entry.itemBody:
An analyst gathers the following liquidity indicators for a company and its peer group:

  Company Peer Group
Quick ratio 0.9 1.1
Operating cycle (days) 70 73
Cash conversion cycle (days) 40 38

All else being equal, the company’s liquidity compares favorably to the peer group based on the:

answerFeedback.85041c64-c68f-4ed8-b7f5-11d4394df5ea: Incorrect because based on the cash conversion cycle, the company’s 40 days is less favorable compared to 38 days for its peer group. A company’s available cash flow is increased by deferring payment to suppliers. This deferral is considered in the net operating cycle, also called the cash conversion cycle, it is a measure of the time from paying suppliers for materials to collecting cash from the subsequent sale of goods produced from these supplies. In general, the shorter these cycles the greater a company’s cash-generating ability and the less its need for liquid assets or outside finance. Because for some liquidity measures a higher number indicates a better position and for some a lower number indicates a better position, the candidate must differentiate and apply that to each of these measures for the company versus the peer group. A candidate who applies the wrong evaluation may choose the wrong measure as being favorable.
answerFeedback.8cbc41ea-9b39-4915-9880-9408a2334db8: Incorrect because the quick ratio for the company, 0.9, is less favorable compared to its peer group at 1.1. The greater the current ratio or the quick ratio (that is, the greater the potential ability to cover current liabilities), the higher a company’s liquidity. Because for some liquidity measures a higher number indicates a better position and for some a lower number indicates a better position, the candidate must differentiate and apply that to each of these measures for the company versus the peer group. A candidate who applies the wrong evaluation may choose the wrong measure as being favorable.
answerFeedback.b5de1846-5c00-462f-9035-fb427526962f: Correct because based on the operating cycle, the company’s 70 days compares favorably to 73 days for its peer group. The operating cycle is a measure of the time needed to convert raw materials into cash from a sale. In general, the shorter these cycles the greater a company’s cash-generating ability and the less its need for liquid assets or outside finance. Of the three measures, the operating cycle is the only measure to which the company has a favorable comparison.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-2020A-CorpFin-Pech-05
entry.itemBody: Which of the following is most likely classified as a drag on liquidity?

answerFeedback.0788cd4e-e70a-4d25-be58-bbdd2825cad0:
Incorrect because a pull on liquidity is when disbursements are paid too quickly or trade credit availability is limited, requiring companies to expend funds before they receive funds from sales that could cover the liability. If suppliers and other vendors who offer credit terms perceive a weakened financial position or are unfamiliar with a company, they may restrict payment terms
so much that the company’s liquidity reserves are stretched thin. Major pulls on payments include limits on short-term lines of credit. If a company’s bank reduces the line of
credit it offers the company, a liquidity squeeze may result. Limits on short-term lines of credit are related to the credit quality of the individual borrower, whereas tight credit market conditions relate to the general market.
answerFeedback.4dc70216-8b82-45b0-889e-39a8003663c1:
Incorrect because a pull on liquidity is when disbursements are paid too quickly or trade credit availability is limited, requiring companies to expend funds before they receive funds from sales that could cover the liability. If suppliers and other vendors who offer credit terms perceive a weakened financial position or are unfamiliar with a company, they may restrict payment terms
so much that the company’s liquidity reserves are stretched thin. Major pulls on payments include reduced credit limits. If a company has a history of making late payments, suppliers may cut the amount of credit they will allow to be outstanding at any time, which can squeeze the company’s liquidity.
answerFeedback.f014c590-8850-43aa-ab4f-e56c45c24fb9:
Correct because a drag on liquidity is when receipts lag, creating pressure from the
decreased available funds. Major drags on receipts involve pressures from credit management and deterioration in other assets such as tight credit. When economic conditions make capital scarcer, short-term debt becomes more expensive to arrange and use.

choices.itemBody: C. Limits on short-term lines of credit

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-08309
entry.itemBody:
An analyst gathers the following information (in $ millions) about three peer companies:

  Year 2 Year 1
Company Credit Sales Average Receivables Balance Credit Sales Average Receivables Balance
1 6.5 3.0 5.0 2.5
2 4.0 1.5 3.0 1.0
3 3.0 1.0 2.5 0.8

Which company reduced the average time to collect accounts receivable between Year 1 and Year 2?

answerFeedback.d6a12d98-c118-43a4-98d6-021235af18d1: Incorrect because the average time taken by Company 2 to collect its accounts receivable increased from 122 days to 137 days. In Year 1 number of days receivable = 1,000,000 / (3,000,000 / 365) = 122 days. In Year 2 number of days receivable = 1,500,000 / (4,000,000 / 365) = 137 days.
answerFeedback.f2bb91fb-e288-4784-a24a-78b46df03943: Correct because the average time it took Company 1 to collect its accounts receivable decreased from 183 days in Year 1 to 168 days in Year 2. Number of days receivable = Accounts receivable / (Sales on credit / 365). In Year 1 number of days receivable = 2,500,000 / (5,000,000 / 365) = 183 days. In Year 2 number of days receivable = 3,000,000 / (6,500,000 / 365) = 168 days.
answerFeedback.f9a906dd-b27c-491c-8740-ff7eeeb9406e: Incorrect because the average time taken by Company 3 to collect its accounts receivable increased from 117 days to 122 days. In Year 1 number of days receivable = 800,000 / (2,500,000 / 365) = 117 days. In Year 2 number of days receivable = 1,000,000 / (3,000,000 / 365) = 122 days.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-09333
entry.itemBody: Which of the following is best described as a secondary source of liquidity?

answerFeedback.421ca080-e77b-4e11-ae09-ead6dbf7ebba: Correct because the main difference between the primary and secondary sources of liquidity is that using a primary source is not likely to affect the normal operations of the company, whereas using a secondary source may result in a change in the company's financial and operating positions. Secondary sources include: negotiating debt contracts, relieving pressures from high interest payments or principal repayments.
answerFeedback.48845c37-4425-4fc0-87b6-ee311da5e27c: Incorrect because bank lines of credit are a primary source of liquidity and not a secondary source of liquidity. Primary sources of liquidity represent the most readily accessible resources available. They may be held as cash or as near-cash securities. Primary sources include short-term funds, which may include items such as trade credit, bank lines of credit, and short-term investment portfolios.
answerFeedback.f70ffec2-d2d0-4d10-a99c-25768268b876: Incorrect because cash flow management is a primary source of liquidity not a secondary source of liquidity. Primary sources of liquidity represent the most readily accessible resources available. They may be held as cash or as near-cash securities. Primary sources include cash flow management, which is the company's effectiveness in its cash management system and practices, and the degree of decentralization of the collections or payments processes.

entry.title: ITEM_CopyofCFA-L1-09336
entry.itemBody:
An analyst gathers the following information about a company:

  Year 1 Year 2
Days sales outstanding 85 76
Days of inventory on hand 136 129
Days payable outstanding 29 13

The company's cash conversion cycle in Year 2 is:

answerFeedback.2c5c4e0e-96ce-436e-9978-bb97cf720f46: Incorrect because in Year 1, the cash conversion cycle was 85 + 136 – 29 = 192 days. In Year 2 the cash conversion cycle was 76 + 129 – 13 = 192 days. Thus, the cash conversion cycle was the same in Year 1 and Year 2.
answerFeedback.cc48adb4-5c73-4107-873c-780566035b2e: Incorrect because the cash conversion cycles are the same.
answerFeedback.d0b80e70-28c3-4c8d-8b0d-3fc019b8c260: Correct because the cash conversion cycle is the same for both years.  The cash conversion cycle equals Days of inventory on hand + Days sales outstanding − Days payable outstanding. In Year 1 the cash conversion cycle was 85 + 136 – 29 = 192 days. In Year 2 the cash conversion cycle was 76 + 129 – 13 = 192 days.

choices.itemBody: A. shorter than the cash conversion cycle in Year 1.
B. the same as the cash conversion cycle in Year 1.
C. longer than the cash conversion cycle in Year 1.

entry.title: ITEM_20170608102
entry.itemBody:
Data for a firm are presented in the following table:
As of 31 December £ Thousands
Cash 200
Accounts receivable 350
Inventory 1,250
Accounts payable 300
Taxes payable 200
Installment loan payable, due in three equal annual payments on 30 June. 600

answerFeedback.0356f415-d209-4d17-857c-37ca60ef2264: Incorrect. The firm’s current ratio is 2.6, which is below the industry average.

Correct. The higher the current ratio, the more liquid the company. Thus, with a current ratio of 2.6 (1,800/700), the company is less liquid than the industry, which has a current ratio of 3.2.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-02280
entry.itemBody: With respect to liquidity management, which of the following activities most likely provides access to a primary source of liquidity?

answerFeedback.53a72190-3312-4575-89d2-7be36873044d: Incorrect because negotiating debt contracts, relieving pressures from high interest payments or principal repayments may signal a company's deteriorating financial health and provide liquidity at a high price. This may well affect the normal operations of the company. Therefore, negotiating debt contracts cannot be a primary source of liquidity.
answerFeedback.a0488d57-b191-44cc-8e3a-d5b1ba39ade2: Correct because primary sources of liquidity are liquidity sources that are the most readily accessible resources available to the company. One of the examples is cash flow management, which is the company's effectiveness in its cash management system and practices, and the degree of decentralization of the collections or payments processes. The more decentralized the system of collections, for example, the more likely the company will be to have cash tied up in the system and not available for use. Therefore, an effective cash management system is a primary source of liquidity as it is likely to be the most readily accessible resources available to the company.
answerFeedback.a9d6f409-96a5-449f-bab9-816d916a6086: Incorrect because the main difference between the primary and secondary sources of liquidity is that using a primary source is not likely to affect the normal operations of the company. However, liquidating assets, which depends on the degree to which short-term and/or long-term assets can be liquidated and converted into cash without substantial loss in value may affect a company's normal operation as productivity is reduced. Therefore, liquidating assets cannot be a primary source of liquidity.

choices.itemBody: B. Creating an effective cash management system
C. Negotiating new debt contracts that delay principal repayment

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-2020-C2-CorpFin-Mazur-07
entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements about sources of liquidity is most accurate?

answerFeedback.2b05d2c8-f3b3-4afe-83d4-2f181a5f27e8: Incorrect because primary sources represent funds that are readily accessible at relatively low cost. On the other hand, use of secondary sources may signal a company’s deteriorating financial health and provide liquidity at a high price - the cost of giving up a company asset to produce emergency cash.
answerFeedback.7a86e3f4-ffdd-47e1-809c-c3067ca1d355: Incorrect because the main difference between the primary and secondary sources of liquidity is that using a primary source is not likely to affect the normal operations of the company, whereas using a secondary source may result in a change in the company’s financial and operating positions.
answerFeedback.9b215bca-a0e6-4728-b689-485c45605f34: Correct because secondary sources include: filing for bankruptcy protection and reorganization. Further, reorganization through bankruptcy, may also be considered a liquidity tool because a company under bankruptcy protection that generates operating cash will be liquid and generally able to continue business operations until a restructuring has been devised and approved.

choices.itemBody: A. Filing for bankruptcy is considered a secondary source of liquidity.
B. Secondary sources of liquidity have a lower cost than primary sources of liquidity.
C. Using a primary source of liquidity impacts the financial and operating positions of a company.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2022.03-CorpIssuers-Lamba-26
entry.itemBody: Which of the following is a pull on a company's liquidity?

answerFeedback.10254d9a-b329-4bb1-999c-10032a6ab848: Incorrect because major drags on receipts involve pressures from credit management and deterioration in other assets and include uncollected receivables. The longer these are outstanding, the greater the risk that they will not be collected at all. They are indicated by the large number of days of receivables and high levels of bad debt expenses. So, uncollected receivables are a drag (not a pull) on a company’s liquidity.
answerFeedback.1d3adfa5-2412-4ccc-b7d1-1f17b2670402: Incorrect because major drags on receipts involve pressures from credit management and deterioration in other assets and include obsolete inventory. If inventory stands unused for long periods, it might be an indication that it is no longer usable. So, obsolete inventory is a drag (not a pull) on a company’s liquidity.
answerFeedback.391f9b94-e27e-4e0c-ad51-62f526153a6c: Correct because a pull on liquidity is when disbursements (outflows) are paid too quickly by the company or trade credit availability is limited, requiring companies to expend funds before they receive funds from sales that could cover the liability. Also, major pulls on payments include reduced credit limits. If a company has a history of making late payments, suppliers might cut the amount of credit they will allow to be outstanding at any time. So, reduced credit limits are a pull on a company’s liquidity.

entry.title: 2027-Mod23-Q1
entry.itemBody: What will be the effect on a direct exchange rate quote if the domestic currency appreciates?

feedback.neutral: B is correct. In the case of a direct exchange rate, the domestic currency is the price currency (the numerator) and the foreign currency is the base currency (the denominator). If the domestic currency appreciates, then fewer units of the domestic currency are required to buy one unit of the foreign currency, and the exchange rate (domestic per foreign) declines. For example, if British pound sterling (GBP) appreciates against the euro (EUR), then euro –sterling (GBP/EUR) might decline.

entry.title: 2027-Mod23-Q2
entry.itemBody: An executive from Switzerland checks into a hotel room in Spain and is told by the manager that EUR1 will buy CHF1.2983. From the executive’s perspective, an indirect exchange rate quote would be:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. An indirect quote takes the foreign country as the price currency and the domestic country as the base currency. To get Swiss francs —which is the executive’s domestic currency—as the base currency, the quote must be stated as EUR/CHF. Using the manager’s information, the indirect exchange rate is (1/1.2983) = 0.7702.

entry.title: 2027-Mod23-Q3
entry.itemBody: Over the past month, the Swiss franc (CHF) has depreciated 12 percent against the British pound (GBP). How much has the pound sterling appreciated against the Swiss franc?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The appreciation of the British pound against the Swiss franc is the inverse of the 12 percent depreciation of the Swiss franc against the pound sterling: [1/(1 – 0.12)] – 1 = (1/0.88) – 1 = 0.1364, or 13.64%.

entry.title: 2027-Mod23-Q4
entry.itemBody: An exchange rate between two currencies has increased to 1.4500. If the base currency has appreciated by 8 percent against the price currency, the initial exchange rate between the two currencies was closest to:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. The percentage appreciation of the base currency can be calculated by dividing the appreciated exchange rate by the initial exchange rate. In this case, the unknown is the initial exchange rate. The initial exchange is the value of X that satisfies the formula: 1.4500/X = 1.08 Solving for X leads to 1.45/1.08 = 1.3426.

entry.title: 2027-Mod23-Q5
entry.itemBody: In the classification of currency regimes, a currency board system (CBS) most likely differs from a fixed-rate parity system in that:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. In a CBS, the monetary authority has an obligation to maintain 100% foreign currency reserves against the monetary base. It therefore cannot lend to troubled financial institutions. As long as the country under a fixed parity regime maintains its exchange peg, the central bank can serve as a lender of last resort.

choices.itemBody: A. a CBS can peg to a basket of currencies but a fixed-rate system cannot.
B. the monetary authority within a CBS does not act as a traditional lender of last resort.
C. a CBS has a discretionary target level of foreign exchange reserves.

entry.title: 2027-Mod23-Q9
entry.itemBody: An analyst gathers the following information: Foreign inflation rate 2% Domestic inflation rate 3% Change in nominal exchange rate 6% Note: the exchange rate is expressed as the number of units of domestic currency per unit of foreign currency. The change in the real exchange rate is closest to:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because the change in the real exchange rate is (1 + ΔSd/f/Sd/f) × (1 + ΔPf/Pf) / (1 + ΔPd/Pd) − 1 = (1 + 6%) × (1 + 2%)/(1 + 3%) − 1 = 1.06 × 1.02/1.03 − 1 = 0.0497 ≈ 0.05 = 5%, where ΔSd/f/Sd/f is the change of the nominal exchange rate, ΔPf/Pf is the foreign inflation rate, and ΔPd/Pd is the domestic inflation rate. Using the appropriate approximate formula, 6.0% + 2.0% – 3.0% = 5% leads to the same answer choice.

entry.title: 2027-Mod23-Q10
entry.itemBody: When a country has a fiscal surplus and an excess of private saving over investment, its exports are:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because using a fundamental identity from macroeconomics, the relationship between the trade balance and expenditure/saving decisions can be expressed as: X– M = (S – I) + (T – G) where X represents exports, M is imports, S is private savings, I is investment in plant and equipment, T is taxes net of transfers, and G is government expenditure. From this relationship, we can see that a trade surplus (X > M) must be reflected in a fiscal surplus (T > G), an excess of private saving over investment (S > I), or both. We can also see that when a country has a fiscal surplus (T > G) and an excess of private saving over investment (S > I), its exports are greater than its imports (X > M).

entry.title: 2027-Mod23-Q11

entry.title: 2027-Mod23-Q12
entry.itemBody: Price levels increase by 2% in the US and by 6% in the Eurozone. If the nominal spot exchange rate of the USD/EUR (amount of US dollars per 1 euro) decreases by 4%, the absolute change in the real exchange rate is closest to:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the change in the real exchange rate is (1 + Δ𝑠𝑑/𝑓 𝑠𝑑/𝑓 ) × (1 + Δ𝑃𝑓 𝑃𝑓 ) (1 + Δ𝑃𝑑 𝑃𝑑 ) − 1 (1 − 4%)× (1 + 6% 1 + 2%) − 1 ≈ 0% Thus, the change in the real exchange rate is approximately zero percent. The rough calculation is: −4% + 6% − 2% = 0%.

entry.title: 2027-Mod23-Q13
entry.itemBody: An ideal international currency regime would most likely have:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the ideal currency regime would have three properties. One of those properties is, all currencies would be fully convertible (i.e., currencies could be freely exchanged for any purpose and in any amount). This condition ensures unrestricted flow of capital. Capital Flows and the FX Market Faculty: Page 6 of 6

entry.title: 2027-Mod23-Q16
entry.itemBody: Assume that the nominal spot exchange rate (USD/EUR) increases by 7.5%, the eurozone price level decreases by 4%, and the US price level increases by 2.5%. The change in the real exchange rate (%) is closest to:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. Real exchange rate = Nominal spot exchange rate × (CPI of the foreign country/CPI of the domestic country) Change in the real exchange rate = [(1 + Change in exchange rate) × (1 + Change in price level in foreign country)]/(1 + Change in price level in domestic country) – 1 = [(1 + 7.5%) × (1 – 4%)]/(1 + 2.5%) – 1 = 0.7%.
